bridge-loans.label: The short answer
bridge-loans.heading: Los Angeles bridge loans: what lenders price and what to plan for

items.q: What do Los Angeles bridge lenders underwrite first?
items.a: The exit. A bridge lender sizes to the takeout, which is a sale, an agency or life company refinance, or CMBS, and then checks that the business plan can reach it on time. On a rent stabilized apartment building the exit is limited by the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, so a realistic renovation and re-leasing schedule matters more than a pro forma that assumes every unit turns. See financing rent controlled apartments in Los Angeles.

items.q: How does Measure ULA affect a bridge loan that ends in a sale?
items.a: Measure ULA is a transfer tax on sales above indexed price thresholds inside the City of Los Angeles. It is a cost at the exit, not at closing, so it belongs in the plan before you choose between selling at stabilization and refinancing into permanent debt. It does not apply outside City limits. The Measure ULA guide walks through the structure, and bridge loan vs permanent refinance compares the two exits.

items.q: Which Los Angeles deals fit a bridge loan?
items.a: Value-add multifamily acquisitions, entitled or unentitled land, properties that need repositioning before they qualify for permanent debt, and purchases with a hard deadline such as a 1031 exchange. See value-add bridge loans, land loans, 1031 exchange bridge loans and bridge to perm.

items.q: Do I need a Los Angeles lender?
items.a: No. Much bridge capital comes from national debt funds and banks. What matters is that the lender has closed Los Angeles collateral and prices the local rules correctly, because a lender who does not will find them in due diligence and re-trade. construction-loans.label: The short answer
construction-loans.heading: Los Angeles construction loans: what decides the quote

items.q: What decides a Los Angeles construction loan quote?
items.a: Entitlement status and the permit stage come first, then the sponsor's track record, the budget and the takeout. A fully entitled site with permits in hand competes for bank and life company construction capital. A site still in discretionary review goes to a smaller group of lenders who accept entitlement risk, and the pricing shows it.

items.q: Which Los Angeles programs change how a project is financed?
items.a: Executive Directive 1 (ED1) speeds approval for 100 percent affordable and supportive housing, which removes discretionary review risk that lenders otherwise price. Transit Oriented Communities (TOC) and density bonus approvals raise the unit count a lender will size to once eligibility is confirmed. Start with the ED1 construction financing guide and the TOC density bonus guide. Conversions are covered in adaptive reuse financing.

items.q: How much leverage can a Los Angeles construction loan reach?
items.a: Conventional construction loans go up to 75 percent of cost. HUD-backed multifamily construction can reach 85 percent. Leverage depends on the sponsor, the entitlements and the lender type.

The loan needs a takeout: a sale, a bridge loan while the building leases up, or permanent debt. Some borrowers choose a single construction to perm loan to avoid a second closing, while others take a separate takeout, which this comparison lays out. Commercial Lending Solutions is a broker, not a lender: we place the loan with the lender that fits your project.

multifamily-loans.label: The short answer
multifamily-loans.heading: Los Angeles multifamily loans: which capital fits which building

items.q: Which lenders finance Los Angeles apartment buildings?
items.a: Stabilized buildings are financed by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, life insurance companies, banks and credit unions, and CMBS. Buildings that are transitional or need renovation start with bridge lenders and debt funds and move to permanent debt after stabilization. Agency loans reach 75 to 80 percent leverage and HUD-backed loans up to 85 percent. See agency loans, HUD and FHA loans, life company loans and multifamily bridge loans.

items.q: How does rent stabilization change underwriting?
items.a: The City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance covers most apartments built before October 1, 1978 and caps annual increases at the percentage the Los Angeles Housing Department publishes each year. Lenders underwrite in-place rents and capped growth, not market rents, and a unit only reprices when it turns. That is why the renovation timeline and expense assumptions carry so much weight. Details are in financing rent controlled apartments in Los Angeles.

items.q: Does Measure ULA affect a multifamily refinance?
items.a: A refinance is not a sale, so it does not trigger the transfer tax. A sale above the indexed thresholds inside the City of Los Angeles does, which is why many owners refinance and hold instead of selling. The Measure ULA guide has the structure.
